findings.evidence: grep '^(namespace|end) ' on the new file yields only `namespace MonoidAlgebra` (109) and `namespace Representation` (135), plus `open TauCeti` (107); by contrast Basic.lean/Orbit.lean have `namespace TauCeti` then `namespace Representation`.
findings.fix: Drop the `TauCeti.` prefix on all references to this file's own declarations (lines 31, 33, 36, 38, 48, 50–53, 58, 60–61, 63, 66–68, 158, 185, 273). Keep it on `conjSubrep` (17), `apply_conjNormal_inv` (146) and `mem_conjSubrep_iff` (329), which really are in `TauCeti.Representation`.
findings.issue: Every docstring reference to a declaration introduced by this file is written `TauCeti.Representation.X`, but the file has no `namespace TauCeti` — line 135 opens `namespace Representation` at the root, so the actual names are `Representation.asModuleTranslate`, `Representation.translateHom`, `Representation.finrank_hom_eq_of_isAtom`, etc. The `## Main definitions` / `## Main statements` index and several inline docstrings therefore point at identifiers that do not exist.

findings.evidence: Basic.lean:111 `theorem apply_conjNormal_inv (g : G) (n : N) (v : V) : ρ g (ρ (MulAut.conjNormal g⁻¹ n : G) v) = ρ (n : G) (ρ g v)`; the new file's own docstring at line 146 says it "is `TauCeti.Representation.apply_conjNormal_inv` read in the other direction".
findings.fix: Derive `apply_conjNormal` from `apply_conjNormal_inv` instead of redoing the group computation, or keep only one statement and update Basic.lean's two uses (`conjSubrep` at 134, `conjSubrepEquiv` at 243).
findings.issue: `Representation.apply_conjNormal` restates `TauCeti.Representation.apply_conjNormal_inv` (Basic.lean:111): substituting `n ↦ MulAut.conjNormal g n` in the latter gives the former. The result is two public lemmas for one identity, in two different namespaces, whose names differ only by an `_inv` suffix — a user has no way to tell which to reach for.

findings.evidence: Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Intertwining.lean:310 `structure Equiv extends IntertwiningMap ρ σ, V ≃ₗ[A] W`, with `Equiv.toLinearEquiv` documented at 315; Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Subrepresentation.lean:106 shows `asSubmodule` reuses `σ.toSubmodule` as its carrier.
findings.fix: Derive `finrank_asSubmodule_conjSubrep` from `(conjSubrepEquiv ρ g σ).toLinearEquiv` — adding the `toSubmodule`/`asSubmodule` carrier bridge to Basic.lean if that reading is needed — and drop `translateSubEquiv`. `translateSub` and its lemmas stay, since `translateHom` genuinely needs them. If `translateSubEquiv` is kept, add `@[simp] coe_translateSubEquiv`.
findings.issue: `translateSubEquiv` adds a second public `k`-linear identification of a subrepresentation with its translate; `TauCeti.Representation.conjSubrepEquiv` (Basic.lean:235) already provides one, since `Representation.Equiv` extends `V ≃ₗ[A] W` and exposes `toLinearEquiv`. `finrank_asSubmodule_conjSubrep` (line 360) is the `finrank` corollary of that existing equivalence. It also ships without any `coe`/`_apply` lemma, so consumers cannot evaluate it without unfolding the structure literal.

findings.evidence: Every sibling characteristic lemma for `conjSubrep` in Basic.lean carries `@[simp]`: `toSubmodule_conjSubrep` (138), `mem_conjSubrep_iff` (143), `conjSubrep_conjSubrep` (169), `conjSubrep_bot` (176), `conjSubrep_top` (181), `isAtom_conjSubrep_iff` (214).
findings.issue: `finrank_hom_conjSubrep` (337) and `finrank_asSubmodule_conjSubrep` (360) are normal-form lemmas — each strictly eliminates a `conjSubrep` from the goal and cannot loop — but neither is tagged `@[simp]`, so `simp` will not reduce a translate's multiplicity or dimension to the original's.

summary: The transport API itself is reasonable, but every docstring reference to this file's own declarations names a non-existent `TauCeti.Representation.*` identifier, and two pieces of the surface (`apply_conjNormal`, `translateSubEquiv`/`finrank_asSubmodule_conjSubrep`) restate public API that already exists in `Clifford/Basic.lean`.
